title: Google ships Gemini 4 Argon — first on Vals, a tie on the index
summary: Google's Gemini 4 Argon leads the board Google chose and ties for eighth on Artificial Analysis's, at an introductory price that matches GPT-6.1 Sol and then doubles. Then decision models go from one startup's bet to everyone's feature in two weeks, including an open clone distilled from Jev's own answers in nine GPU hours. And America.gov answers obscure records without inventing anything, then stops answering the 2020 election overnight.

topics: Gemini 4 Argon: Google claims first on the Vals Index and SOTA on DeepSWE v1.1 (77.9%), 68% tied-first on CWE-bench v1; Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 53 (#8/223), tied with Fable 5.1 and Astra max, below Opus 5.5 (58 max); introductory $2/$10 per million matching GPT-6.1 Sol, rising to $4/$20; 110M output tokens to run the index vs 82M median; Fairwind-first rollout without cyber guardrails for defenders; 1M output-token limit

Decision models commoditize in two weeks: OpenAI's Decisions API (Luna weights, reasoning off, priced as Luna, built in about a week), Ollama 0.35 system-one endpoint with Nimble 9B at 91 ms on an M5 Max, Liquid d1, and AutoTrust's open JEV-27B — a detachable LoRA plus decision head on frozen Qwen3.8-27B, distilled from Jev's own output distributions in ~9.2 B200 hours, mean 84.07 vs Jev 1.13's 83.85 on the authors' six-benchmark run

America.gov: GSA's Gemini- and Grok-powered federal chatbot; Newsweek's launch-day answers on the 2020 election, impeachments and conviction; a reporter group's 15-question records test (9 correct, 6 incomplete, zero hallucinations); the overnight switch to 'I do not provide political commentary' reported via CNN's Daniel Dale; FirstGov-to-USA.gov lineage and evaluation as a snapshot of a mutable configuration

dives.why_it_matters: Anyone choosing a frontier model this quarter needs the independent number and the post-introductory price, not the launch-post board.
Agent builders replacing slow LLM classification loops now have local, open and OpenAI options, and the distilled clone shows what a decision model's moat is and isn't.
